newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Luz del Sur sale draws $155 mln - source.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Luz del Sur sale draws $155 mln - source.

text.p: The government's share placement of its 30 percent stake in Luz del Sur has drawn offers from Peruvian individual investors worth more than 400 million soles ($155 million), a source close to the sale said Wednesday.
The sale's managers intended to distribute only 240 million soles worth of shares in the electricity distributor to individuals, the banking source added.

The government, hoping to raise -- at home and abroad -- a total of $200 million from the sale, has said it will distribute 55 percent of the shares sold through the placement to Peruvian individuals.

Under a scheme known as Citizens' Participation in Privatization, where nationals receive up to a 10 percent discount, individuals had two weeks to offer to buy shares before the program's end November 29.
"Due to the incredible success, it is clear the process of distributing the shares is going to leave a lot of unsatisfied demand," the source said.

In July, there was so much unsatisfied local demand in the placement of state-held shares in Telefonica del Peru that the government was forced to sell a further three percent stake in the company after the original offer closed.
In the Luz del Sur sale, the government expects institutional investors at home and abroad to buy the remaining 45 percent of the placement's shares, whose price will be set on December 10.
The government will define the distribution of the shares it sells on December 13.
Officials from investment bank CS First Boston -- chosen by the government to handle the international portion of the sale -- said they expected the placement abroad to raise about $100 million.
The domestic portion of the sale was divided into two parts.
In the sale of shares to individual Peruvian nationals, Banco Continental directed a group of local banks that includes Banco de Credito, Interbanc and Banco Wiese.

In the second part of the local sale, Spain's Banco Santander was selected to handle the placement with local institutions. The Spanish bank's brokerage in Peru - Santander SAB - will direct a group of local brokerages to book build with institutions such as local pension funds, insurance companies and banks.

In June 1994, a consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc. and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc. bought a 60 percent stake in Luz del Sur, a former state-run electricity company for $212.1 million.
Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.
